mainTopic: Why רב calls a woman a בעולה and not a זונה; relations with an animal and fitness for כהונה; a כהן גדול who marries an אנוסה or מפותה
overview: Earlier, רב ruled that a woman who had relations שלא כדרכה may not marry a כהן גדול, because she counts as a בעולה. A ברייתא seemed to disagree. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, while רב follows רבי אלעזר. But according to רבי אלעזר such a woman would already be a זונה, so why did רב mention בעולה? רב יוסף suggests the case of an animal. אביי rejects that answer, so רבי זירא says רב meant a ממאנת, who is a בעולה but not a זונה. The גמרא then rules that relations with an animal leave a woman fit for כהונה, and even for a כהן גדול. It supports this with a ברייתא, a story about רבי, and a פסוק read through a משנה about אתנן and מחיר. Finally, a ברייתא teaches about a כהן גדול who marries an אנוסה or מפותה. רב says he must divorce her, and the defense of רב continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, while רב follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The proof against רב is pushed aside. The ברייתא reflects רבי מאיר's view, and רב holds like רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי מאיר's. And רב, when he spoke, was following רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא. It says the ברייתא and רב are simply following two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to allow this woman to marry a כהן גדול, which would go against רב. The גמרא says that ברייתא is רבי מאיר's view. רבי אלעזר disagrees with רבי מאיר, and רב follows רבי אלעזר, so the ברייתא is no proof against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? (asking which תנא a source follows)

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is רבי מאיר's,
and רב, who said his ruling, spoke like רבי אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof from the ברייתא that came before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא against רב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא follows only one side of a מחלוקת (רבי מאיר). רב follows the other side (רבי אלעזר).

steps.title: If רב follows רבי אלעזר, why call her a בעולה instead of a זונה?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אלעזר, any relations outside marriage make a woman a זונה. So why did רב need to use the reason of בעולה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If רב follows רבי אלעזר, why did he give the reason that she is a בעולה? He could have said she is a זונה! After all, רבי אלעזר said that an unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman, not for the sake of marriage, makes her a זונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If רב follows רבי אלעזר, his reason seems strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that relations outside marriage make a woman a זונה, who is forbidden to every כהן. If so, this woman should be forbidden as a זונה. Then the narrower reason רב gave, בעולה, seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? (why choose this reason?)
Let him derive it from (there is an easier reason)
A woman who is no longer a virgin
A woman forbidden to marry any כהן
For the sake of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Here זונה is a legal status that makes a woman forbidden to a כהן. It does not mean what the English word usually means.

phrases.english: If he follows רבי אלעזר,
why specifically because she is a non-virgin?
Let him derive it from the fact that she is a זונה!
For רבי אלעזר said:
An unmarried man who has relations with an unmarried woman
not for the sake of marriage
has made her a זונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, מַאי אִירְיָא מִשּׁוּם בְּעוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 1 that רב follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's choice of the reason בעולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי אלעזר she is already a זונה, a broader disqualification, so the reason בעולה is not needed.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a case where she is a בעולה but not a זונה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רב is speaking of relations with an animal. That makes her a בעולה but not a זונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב means a case where she had relations with an animal. There, the reason of בעולה applies, but the reason of זונה does not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. He gives a specific case where only the reason of בעולה works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a זונה, even under רבי אלעזר, comes from relations with a man. With an animal there is no man involved, so she is not a זונה. She is still not a virgin, so רב had to use the reason of בעולה.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as (narrowing to a specific case)
There is / there is not
An animal

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
For example, where she had relations with an animal,
for there, the reason of non-virgin applies,
but the reason of זונה does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּבְעֲלָה לִבְהֵמָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling covers ordinary relations with a man, so זונה should have been the reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling is about relations with an animal. That makes her a בעולה only, not a זונה.

steps.title: אביי: בעולה and זונה go together either way
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the two statuses cannot be split. Either she is both a בעולה and a זונה, or she is neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Whichever way you look at it, there is a problem. If she counts as a non-virgin, she is also a זונה. And if she is not a זונה, she is also not a non-virgin.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer. He uses a two-sided argument that leaves no way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף tried to make the animal case count for בעולה but not for זונה. אביי says this is inconsistent. If the act counts as real relations, it should create both statuses. If it does not count, it should create neither.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you take it (a two-sided argument)
Also
She is (she counts as)

phrases.english: אביי said to him: Whichever way you take it:
If she is a non-virgin,
she is also a זונה.
And if she is not a זונה,
she is also not a non-virgin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's split between בעולה and זונה in the animal case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The act either counts as relations or it does not. Both statuses depend on the same question, so one cannot exist without the other.

steps.title: אביי rejects a comparison to מוכת עץ
steps.stepSummary: אביי blocks a possible defense comparing this case to מוכת עץ שלא כדרכה. If that counted as losing virginity, no woman would be fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say it is like a woman who was struck by an object in an unusual way: if so, you have no woman fit for כהונה, since every woman may have been struck that way by a small stone.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי expects that someone might defend רב יוסף with a comparison. He knocks down that comparison right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A defender might say: just as מוכת עץ loses her virginity without becoming a זונה, the same could be true here. אביי answers that מוכת עץ שלא כדרכה cannot make a woman unfit. If it did, every woman would be unfit, since this can happen through something as ordinary as a pebble. So the comparison fails, and אביי's question on רב יוסף still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (expecting a defense)
It is just like (making a comparison)
A woman whose virginity was damaged by an object, not by a man
Not in the usual way
A small stone, a pebble

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's answer (the animal case) is under serious attack. According to אביי, בעולה and זונה stand or fall together. The comparison to מוכת עץ cannot save the answer, because otherwise every woman would be unfit for כהונה.

phrases.english: And if you will say:

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵי דְּהָוֵיא אַמוּכַּת עֵץ שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ,
phrases.english: It is just like a woman struck by an object not in the usual way,
phrases.notes: Literally "struck by wood." It means a woman who lost her virginity through an object, not through a man.

phrases.english: if so, you have no woman
who is fit for the priesthood,
who did not become struck by an object
through a pebble.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מִידֵי דְּהָוֵיא אַמוּכַּת עֵץ שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens אביי's question in step 4 by closing off a possible defense of רב יוסף.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects comparing the animal case to מוכת עץ שלא כדרכה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If מוכת עץ שלא כדרכה made a woman a בעולה, every woman would be unfit for כהונה, which cannot be.

steps.title: רב was speaking about a girl who refused her husband
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא drops the animal case and says רב was talking about a ממאנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי זירא said: רב was talking about a girl who refused her husband (a ממאנת).
steps.whatsHappening: The animal answer has just been knocked down, so רבי זירא offers a new case to explain why רב used the reason of בעולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממאנת was married when the relations happened, so they were not forbidden relations and she is not a זונה. But she is no longer a virgin, so she is a בעולה. This finally gives a case where she is a בעולה without being a זונה, which answers the question from Step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given
A girl married off as a minor by her mother or brothers who refuses the marriage, which ends it
A woman who is no longer a virgin

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being a בעולה and being a זונה are two separate things after all. They can be split apart, just not in the way רב יוסף suggested.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Zeira said:
It is about a girl who refused her husband.
phrases.notes: She had relations with her husband while they were married, so it was not זנות, but she is no longer a virgin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's animal case, which אביי rejected in Steps 4-5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב must have meant relations with an animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant a ממאנת, who is a בעולה but not a זונה.

steps.title: A woman who had relations with an animal stays fit for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא rules that relations with an animal do not disqualify a woman from marrying a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said: A woman who had relations with an animal is still fit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: relations with an animal do not make a woman unfit for כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with an animal are not זנות, so she does not become a זונה and may still marry a regular כהן. רב שימי בר חייא speaks only about a regular כהן. Whether she also stays fit for a כהן גדול is taken up in Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: She had relations with an animal
Fit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said:
A woman who had relations with an animal
is fit for the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the animal case that came up in the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with an animal do not disqualify a woman from כהונה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ruling even though the act is a capital sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same ruling and adds that this holds even though the act can bring the death penalty of סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: If a woman had relations with one who is not a man, even though she can be punished with stoning, she is still fit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב שימי בר חייא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the point stronger: the act is a very serious sin, punishable by סקילה, yet it still does not make her a זונה. How severe a sin is does not decide whether it is זנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this; used to support the statement just made
One who is not a man; here, an animal
Stoning, a death penalty of בית דין

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that a sin punishable by death must disqualify her from כהונה. The ברייתא says the opposite: being fit for כהונה depends on זנות, not on how serious the sin is.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
If she had relations with one who is not a man,
even though it is punishable by stoning,
she is fit for the priesthood.

steps.raayaObject: רב שימי בר חייא's ruling that relations with an animal do not disqualify her from כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about one who had relations with 'one who is not a man'

steps.title: A real case: רבי permitted a girl attacked by a dog
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי ruled a girl attacked by a dog was still fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: There was a story about a girl in היתלו who was sweeping the house. A village dog attacked her from behind, and רבי ruled she was fit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real story where this הלכה was actually applied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ruling is backed by an actual decision of רבי, not only by a statement and a ברייתא. Because the act was with an animal, it was not זנות, so she stayed fit for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A story about something that really happened
A young girl
A village dog

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
There was an incident with a certain girl in Hitlu
who was sweeping the house,
and a village dog had relations with her from behind,
and Rabbi declared her fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרִיבָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a real-life ruling that matches Steps 7-8.
steps.raayaObject: That relations with an animal do not disqualify a woman from כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about רבי's ruling, reported by רב דימי

steps.title: שמואל: She was permitted even to a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: שמואל adds that רבי permitted the girl even to a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: And she was permitted even to a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds to the story: the girl was fit even for a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may only marry a בתולה, which is stricter than the rule for a regular כהן. שמואל is saying that the animal act does not even take away her status as a בתולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest, who may only marry a בתולה
A virgin

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
And even to a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי's ruling in Step 9 to a כהן גדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She keeps her status as a בתולה and may marry a כהן גדול.

steps.title: There was no כהן גדול in רבי's time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל could say this, since there was no כהן גדול in the days of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there a כהן גדול in the days of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's words, because the בית המקדש was already destroyed in רבי's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no בית המקדש there was no serving כהן גדול. So it seems strange to say רבי permitted her to marry one.

keyTerms.meaning: Was there? A question that expects the answer 'no'

phrases.aramaic: בִּימֵי רַבִּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מִי הֲוָה?
phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi, was there a High Priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימֵי רַבִּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of שמואל's addition in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that רבי permitted her to a כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There was no כהן גדול after the חורבן, so the statement cannot be meant literally.

steps.title: She is fit for a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל meant she has the status of one who is fit for a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant she is fit for a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל was describing her status, not an actual marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was not saying a כהן גדול was really allowed to marry her then. He meant that by הלכה she counts as a בתולה, so if there were a כהן גדול she could marry him.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit; has the proper status

phrases.english: Rather, she is fit for a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by reading שמואל's words differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל meant she was actually permitted to a serving כהן גדול.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל meant she has the status of one fit for a כהן גדול.
steps.whatToRemember: Relations with an animal do not make a woman a זונה, and they do not even take away her status as a בתולה. She is fit for a regular כהן and even for a כהן גדול.

steps.title: What is the source that there is no זנות with an animal?
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזקיא asks רב אשי where the חכמים learned that relations with an animal are not זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מפרזקיא said to רב אשי: Where do we learn what the חכמים said, that there is no זנות with an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ruling is clear, רבא מפרזקיא asks for its source in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything so far assumed that an animal does not make a woman a זונה. Now the גמרא looks for the פסוק behind this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn this?
Relations with an animal do not count as זנות

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזַקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava of Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:
From where is this matter derived
that the Sages said,
there is no harlotry with an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling taught in Steps 7-12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches there is no זנות with an animal

steps.title: The source: the hire of a זונה and the price of a dog
steps.stepSummary: The answer quotes the פסוק that forbids bringing a זונה's payment or the price of a dog to the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "You shall not bring the hire of a harlot or the price of a dog."
steps.whatsHappening: The answer gives a פסוק as the source; the גמרא will explain how it proves the point in the lines that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids bringing to the מזבח an animal given as payment to a זונה, or one given in exchange for a dog. The source is set up here, and the explanation of how it teaches 'no זנות with an animal' comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a זונה
The price of a dog; something given in exchange for a dog

phrases.english: As it is written:
"You shall not bring the hire of a harlot
or the price of a dog."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: לֹא תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 by quoting a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of אתנן זונה ומחיר כלב is the source; how it proves the point is explained next.

steps.title: Only the two cases in the verse are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that a 'dog's hire' and a 'זונה's price' may be brought as offerings, because the פסוק says 'both of them,' which means only two cases are forbidden, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: the hire of a dog and the price of a זונה are permitted, because it says 'both of them': two, and not four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up the פסוק from the last step. The verse forbids only exactly the two cases it names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids a זונה's hire and a dog's price. The reverse cases, payment given to a dog's owner for relations with the animal and the price paid for a זונה, are allowed. Since payment for relations with an animal is not treated as a זונה's hire, relations with an animal are not זנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given for forbidden relations
Price paid when buying or trading something
'Both of them', a phrase in the פסוק that limits the rule to two cases

steps.whatToRemember: The verse forbids only a זונה's hire and a dog's price, not the reverse. So payment for relations with an animal is not a זונה's hire, and relations with an animal are not זנות.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the switch: the פסוק says 'hire of a זונה' and 'price of a dog,' while the משנה permits the reverse, 'hire of a dog' and 'price of a זונה.'

phrases.english: And we learned: the hire of a dog
phrases.notes: This means payment given to a dog's owner so a person could have relations with the animal.

phrases.english: and the price of a prostitute are permitted,
because it is stated: "both of them"
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: two, and not four.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: אֶתְנַן כֶּלֶב וּמְחִיר זוֹנָה מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from step 14 by bringing a משנה that reads the פסוק narrowly.
steps.raayaObject: That relations with an animal are not זנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה reading 'גם שניהם' as limiting the rule to exactly two cases

steps.title: A כהן גדול who marries a woman who was raped or seduced
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a כהן גדול may not marry a woman he raped or seduced, but if he did, the marriage holds. If another man raped or seduced her, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the child is a חלל and the חכמים say the child is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a woman he himself raped or seduced, he may not marry, but if he married her, he is married. A woman raped or seduced by another man, he may not marry. If he did marry her, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the child is a חלל, and the חכמים say the child is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about whom a כהן גדול may marry. It splits the cases into a woman he himself was with and a woman another man was with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases he may not marry her from the start. The ברייתא then gives different results after the fact: for his own אנוסה or מפותה it says 'he is married,' and for another man's, the תנאים argue about whether the child is a חלל.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was raped
A woman who was seduced
A child of a כהן who loses כהונה status because of a forbidden marriage
Fit, with unflawed lineage

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
a woman he himself raped and a woman he himself seduced
he may not marry,
phrases.notes: 'He' is a כהן גדול, who must marry a בתולה.

phrases.english: and if he married her, he is married.
a woman raped by another and a woman seduced by another
he may not marry, and if he married her,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: הַוָּלָד חָלָל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: the child is a chalal,
and the Rabbis say: the child is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֲנוּסַת עַצְמוֹ וּמְפוּתַּת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on a related topic of whom a כהן גדול may marry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול may not marry an אנוסה or מפותה. If she was his own, 'he is married.' If she was another man's, there is a dispute over whether the child is a חלל.

steps.title: רב rules that he must still divorce her
steps.stepSummary: On the words 'if he married, he is married,' רב הונא quotes רב: he must still divorce her with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he married her, he is married': רב הונא said in the name of רב, and he must send her away with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא, and רב adds that the כהן גדול must divorce her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'he is married' as saying only that the marriage takes effect, so a גט is needed to end it. It does not mean the couple may stay together.

keyTerms.meaning: Must send her away with a bill of divorce
Married, meaning the marriage takes effect

phrases.english: "If he married her, he is married":
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא's ruling about a woman he himself raped or seduced.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
and he must send her away with a get.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נָשָׂא נָשׂוּי, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an explanation to a line in the ברייתא from step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even though the marriage takes effect, he must divorce her with a גט.

steps.title: The wording seems to mean he may stay married
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: the ברייתא says 'if he married, he is married,' which sounds like he may stay married to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about what the ברייתא teaches, 'if he married her, he is married'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב using the ברייתא's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the marriage taking effect is too obvious to need saying. So the words 'he is married' must be teaching that he may keep her, which goes against רב's ruling that he must divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: But then, which opens a challenge
That which it teaches

phrases.english: But then, that which it teaches:
"If he married her, he is married"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּקָתָנֵי: אִם נָשָׂא נָשׂוּי
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that he must divorce her with a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'He is married' sounds like he may stay with her. Otherwise the phrase would be saying something obvious.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב begins to explain the wording
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב starts to explain what 'he is married' comes to teach. His answer continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: it comes to say...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב begins his defense of רב. Only the opening word appears here, and the rest of his answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He will show that 'he is married' teaches something that still fits with the requirement to give a גט. So far, only his opening is given.

keyTerms.meaning: To say, meaning 'it comes to teach'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לוֹמַר
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: it comes to say

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge from step 18.
